searchText: Hello, Hope everyone is doing great. I am bit curious about pre-allocated balance 1 eth in `genesis.json` for any `merge-devnet`. Why did we define pre-allocated balance 1 eth? https://github.com/eth-clients/merge-testnets/blob/773f8bc7b83c696831746e1ff15a30fcf75bea1e/merge-devnet-5/genesis.json#L17 Why did we defined pre-allocated storage for deposit contract? (https://github.com/eth-clients/merge-testnets/blob/773f8bc7b83c696831746e1ff15a30fcf75bea1e/merge-devnet-5/genesis.json#L789) pre-allocated balances were for precompiles if i'm not wrong. The pre-allcoated storage for the deposit contract was to ensure its present at genesis, that way we could spin up the PoW and PoS chain together, instead of having to wait for the PoW chain to be up and then deploy a deposit contract to it. Thanks <@199561711278227457> . Did we pre-allocate the 1 eth for any special reason? Are there any plans to set up a permissionless Merge testnet (like Ropsten on PoW where anyone could join the network regardless of anything), or convert existing permissioned testnet into permissionless? I think anyone can join Goerli after the merge. You can currently set up a validator on Prater to test the merge transition. It's 1 Wei, not 1 ETH, and as <@199561711278227457> says, it's for precompiles. This has a rather interesting history: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/issues/716#issuecomment-330824096 - it avoids the precompiles being seen as "empty" accounts, which got us into trouble once upon a time. prater/goerli and ropsten also merged a while ago While you can run a validator or two on Goerli, you can’t run thousands of them. So it’s still permissioned to some extent You can most certainly run thousands, just need the goeth An entity that has a reason to run thousands and can commit to keeping them up will also be able to get that goeth Ropsten is permissioned as there are 100k genesis validators, and you can’t really become a significant part of the validation set without having the rETH premine “just”. I think a fully permissionless testnet with no genesis validator set and no premine will make a decent simulation of mainnet. I figured it would be nice one to have for people to try attacking. It would help find flaws in security, and harden the merge design as much as possible. That actually makes for a relatively 💩 simulation of mainnet, as we've seen during Medalla. All that happens is that people walk away from their validators because there's no incentive to keep them running ... 1 GöETH == 0 USD ... and the network goes into non-finality, bleeds out validators, reaches finality, rinse-repeat. Same thing with attack scenarios: The ones that could have been thought of, have been thought of and have been tested. If you have a novel scenario, by all means bring it. There will be resources to test it, on that testnet or any other. Testing for the merge is done. That's what the mainnet shadow forks are for. Ongoing testing post-merge is always interesting. As for availability of GöETH, the solo staking community and ethstaker feel the pain. I like the idea of making Görli LUNA again by minting (irregular state change) 4 trillion of it. That would allow us to greatly relax Sybil resistance on the faucet, and we could just out-amount the farmers. Greatly relaxed Sybil resistance on the ethstaker Görli faucet might look like this: BrightID optional (maybe higher limits with it), otherwise 32.1 GöETH every 28 days to every Discord account >= 2 weeks old. We can quibble about exact amounts and that'll depend on how large the farming drain is. **If** the LUNA-fication of Görli even happens. If we LUNA-fy Görli I am happy to personally lobby for sending you 32010 so you can run your 1,000 attack validators :). We need another testnet you say Doesn't help It's early and I am just having coffee so I'll indulge both of us by briefly going into the pickle we're in, and why another testnet doesn't solve it. Görli farmers are "rational actors", they want to make a buck. For this they need Görli to have value. This can be achieved by creating scarcity: Drain faucets and force them into ever-more-onerous Sybil resistance You then end up with people willing to pay for Görli because they don't want to deal with PoW or BrightID to get test ETH This works the same with any testnet It is (nearly) free to drain faucets, hence it is rational to do so and attempt to create scarcity and thus value Shadow forks are 1) somewhat private (no one asks to join them) 2) low peer count, most of nodes are maintained by the EF And as for Goerli, PoS is always *permissioned* if there is no way to get native ETH without asking people from EF or related entities. <@354681205842771973> if you want goerli eth, i can sell you some for EthPOW coins (assuming replayable) <:killmelmao:818203990768091137>
